item.description: President Trump is making changes to his inner circle that signal how he may approach divided government.

item.title: How will Democrats approach foreign policy after their midterm win?
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Thomas Wright, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, about his piece in Foreign Affairs titled The Fight for the Future of Democratic Foreign Policy.

item.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
item.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

item.title: NPR's Moscow and Beijing correspondents discuss the reaction to U.S. elections abroad
item.description: The results of the U.S. midterms were closely followed overseas. NPR correspondents in Moscow and Beijing discuss how the elections are seen in the countries they cover.

item.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.

item.title: Historically red state legislatures have flipped. Here's what's on their agenda
item.description: Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.

item.title: Week in politics: Democrats plan for the next Congress, Trump's new Chief of Staff
item.description: Democrats plans for the next Congress, where they'll hold significant majorities in both chambers. Meanwhile, President Trump signals his plans by promoting Stephen Miller as his new Chief of Staff.

item.title: How Gen Z voters helped fuel a blue wave for Democrats
item.description: Republicans made gains with young voters in 2024, but in this year's midterms Americans under 30 issued a strong rebuke of President Trump and his party, voting decisively for Democrats instead.
